Cold stratification. Basically mimicking the winter dormancy they would go through to prevent seeds in fall from immediately germinating and dying in winter. Some needs a few weeks, some need repeated freeze and thaw cycles. Some need to be heated to grass fire temperatures, some to forest fire temps. There's also acid scarification, to mimic digestion as the seeds would normally need to be eaten by animals and carried away from the mother plant so they don't compete.
